rationale: dual_domain_supervised-claude-agentic: unet_c=16, lr=0.00015, epochs=10, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=579, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-7 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). BASE_ITER=6 (the CHAMPION: unet_c=16/lr=1e-4/epochs=10/train_n=579/lambda_neg=1.0/grad_clip=1.0/seed=42, hr 0.415794, the campaign Mayo champion). ONE KNOB (optimization): lr 1e-4 -> 1.5e-4 (everything else identical: unet_c=16, epochs=10, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=579, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, seed=42). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) iter-6 champion: SSIM 0.93261 / hr 0.415794 at ep10/train_n=579/c16/lr1e-4, elapsed_s=1172.0s (19.5 min, only ~28s headroom inside the 1200s wall). Measured per-epoch on the full 579-slice pool from iter-5 (ep9, 1082.1s) + iter-6 (ep10, 1172.0s): (1172.0-1082.1)/(10-9)=89.9 s/epoch marginal, fixed=1172.0-10*89.9=273s (data load + 214-slice per-sample val + figure). (2) LIMITER: epochs are WALL-PINNED at 10 (ep10 used 1172/1200s; ep11=273+11*89.9=1262s=21.0min BUSTS the 20-min wall). Data coverage MAXED (train_n=579 = entire Wagner pool, cannot rise). Capacity bump is UNFUNDABLE: the wall is pinned at ep10 with zero spare epochs to trade, and iter-4 already showed c24 REGRESSED to 0.29856 precisely because trading epochs to fund 2.25x conv-compute under-trained the bigger net -- with no epochs to spare now, c24 would under-train even worse. So the only within-budget lever left is OPTIMIZATION. lr has NEVER been tuned in this campaign (fixed at 1e-4 across all 6 iters); no lr-schedule is wired (FORBIDDEN to edit the shared solver), so a constant-lr change is the only optimization lever. The hr trajectory is still CLIMBING (ep8/n200 0.276 -> ep20 0.339 -> ep27 0.3654 -> ep9/n579 0.3994 -> ep10/n579 0.4158, +0.0164 on the last epoch step) -> the net is EPOCH-STARVED on the full pool (only 10 passes), NOT at a convergence plateau. (3) ONE KNOB: lr 1e-4 -> 1.5e-4. This makes each of the 10 epochs do more effective work (directly attacks the epoch-starvation limiter) at ZERO extra compute -- an lr change does not alter per-epoch cost, so the pinned wall stays safe (no epoch trade needed; this is precisely why lr is chosen over capacity). 1.5e-4 is a 50pct bump, well under the 5e-4 that NaN-ed standalone; grad_clip=1.0 + nonfinite-grad-skip remain the NaN guard. (4) HYPOTHESIS: lr 1e-4->1.5e-4 lifts hr ABOVE 0.415794, because the full-pool net is epoch-starved at 10 passes and a 50pct larger stable step lets each pass converge further (the epochs slope was still positive at the wall). FALSIFIER (in NUMBERS): if hr <= 0.415794 at lr=1.5e-4 (plateau, drop, or NaN-skip instability), then 1e-4 was already the optimal stable step at this budget and dual_domain_supervised is at its DEFINITIVE BUDGET-CONSTRAINED Mayo CEILING (0.4158, the campaign Mayo CHAMPION) -- all four within-budget levers exhausted: epochs (wall-locked at 10), data (maxed at 579), capacity (regressed iter-4, unfundable now), and lr (this iter). PREDICTED iter-7 hr ~0.420-0.425. (5) BUDGET: lr change does NOT alter per-epoch cost -> ep10/train_n=579 stays ~1172s (19.5 min), inside the 1200s train+score wall and the 30-min sbatch wall; no epoch trade. (6) no control return. HARD-WIRED (unchanged): staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP + per-sample pipe.R_full swap, bg_target=truth, metric=321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override).
